title: Northwind Industrial: public comps and valuation summary
subtitle: Board valuation update
note: All figures are synthetic and illustrative.

slides.title: Triangulated enterprise value is $912m to $980m, or 9.5x to 10.2x FY26E EBITDA
bullets: Trading comps imply 8.5x to 10.5x FY26E EBITDA of $96.0m, or $816m to $1,008m
Precedent transactions imply 9.5x to 11.5x LTM EBITDA, or $912m to $1,104m
DCF at 9.0% to 10.0% WACC implies $880m to $1,090m
Northwind trades at 9.1x, a 0.4x discount to the peer median of 9.5x
The discount is explained by lower margin (17.1% vs 19.5% median), not growth
slides.source: FactSet, company filings, as of 30 Oct 2026

slides.title: Peers trade at a median 9.5x EV/EBITDA; Northwind sits 0.4x below on a lower margin
slides.source: FactSet consensus, 30 Oct 2026; Northwind management case

slides.title: Northwind ranks sixth of nine on EV/EBITDA, level with Ember and ahead of Delta and Granite
All four methods overlap between $912m and $980m, supporting a midpoint near $946m
Recent precedents cleared 9.5x to 11.5x LTM EBITDA, with strategic buyers at the top
Closing the 2.4-point margin gap to peers is worth roughly $130m of enterprise value at the peer median multiple
bullets: Each 100 bps of margin adds about $53m of EV ($561m revenue x 1% x 9.5x)
Cost programme targets 230 bps by FY28, closing the gap almost in full
Mix shift to aftermarket (28% to 35% of sales) supports the upper half of the range
Re-rating is not in our base case; we value at the 9.1x current multiple

slides.title: Methodology: consensus EBITDA, last-twelve-month precedents and a five-year DCF
bullets: Peer set: eight US and European industrial manufacturers, $1bn to $6bn EV
Multiples use enterprise value at 30 Oct 2026 close and FactSet consensus
DCF: five-year explicit period, 2.0% terminal growth, mid-year convention
Excluded: two peers with pending M&A and one with restated FY25 results
